title: ICAB C1 - Accounting
summary: Covers double-entry accounting principles, recording transactions, adjustments, preparation of financial statements for sole traders, partnerships, and limited companies under IFRS, and public financial management fundamentals.

all.name: Full Syllabus Tracker
all.blurb: Official 2025 Syllabus chapter and topic tracker for Accounting. Track your study progress across all syllabus areas.

stages.title: Area 1: Accounting Concepts, Ethics & Sustainability
stages.name: Area 1: Accounting Concepts, Ethics & Sustainability
stages.description: IFRS Conceptual Framework, qualitative characteristics, accounting principles, and ISSB sustainability disclosures.

nodes.name: Conceptual Framework & Standard Setting
nodes.description: Standard-setting process used by IASB and local authorities (FRC/ICAB); qualitative characteristics of financial information; effects of transactions under the Conceptual Framework; true and fair view override.
topics: IASB standard-setting structure and Bangladesh endorsement process
Fundamental qualitative characteristics: Relevance and Faithful Representation
Enhancing characteristics: Comparability, Verifiability, Timeliness, Understandability
Elements of financial statements: Asset, Liability, Equity, Income, Expense
Concepts of 'fair presentation' and 'true and fair view'
learningOutcomes: Understand the standard-setting process used by IASB and local authority.
Identify the qualitative characteristics of financial information.
Apply recognition and derecognition criteria to business events.
checklists: Read Conceptual Framework chapter in ICAB Manual
Practice 20 objective questions on qualitative characteristics
Summarize True and Fair view criteria in revision notebook
resources: Relevant Acts & Standards (IFRS / ISA / Tax Acts)

nodes.name: Ethics & Sustainability in Reporting
nodes.description: Professional ethics under IESBA Code, ICAB Bye-laws on misconduct, and introduction to IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards (ISSB S1/S2).
topics: IESBA Code of Ethics fundamental principles: Integrity, Objectivity, Professional Competence, Confidentiality, Professional Behaviour
Professional misconduct prescribed by ICAB bye-laws
Principles-based vs rules-based ethical reasoning
Introduction to sustainability in financial reporting and ISSB aims (IFRS S1 & S2)
Stakeholder information needs regarding climate and ESG impacts
learningOutcomes: Specify ethical considerations for preparers of financial statements.
Identify professional misconduct rules under ICAB bye-laws.
Explain the aims of ISSB and how standards meet investor information needs.
checklists: Memorize 5 IESBA ethical principles and threats/safeguards
Review ICAB bye-laws regarding disciplinary procedures
Understand basic scope of IFRS S1 General Requirements
resources: Relevant Acts & Standards (IFRS / ISA / Tax Acts)

stages.title: Area 2: Maintaining Financial Records
stages.name: Area 2: Maintaining Financial Records
stages.description: Double-entry bookkeeping techniques, books of prime entry, ledger accounting, and transaction recording.

nodes.name: Double Entry Techniques & Prime Entry
nodes.description: Why entities maintain financial records; sources of financial information; sales, purchases, cash books, petty cash and general journals.
topics: Purpose of maintaining records: Stewardship, tax compliance, management control
Books of prime entry: Sales daybook, Purchases daybook, Returns daybooks
Cash book, two-column and three-column formats, Petty cash imprest system
General journal entries for non-routine transactions
Trade discounts vs cash discounts recording
learningOutcomes: Specify why entities maintain financial records and prepare statements.
Identify sources of information for accounting records.
Record transactions across prime books into general ledger.
checklists: Solve 15 practical exercises on books of prime entry
Balance off ledger accounts and extract initial trial balance
resources: Relevant Acts & Standards (IFRS / ISA / Tax Acts)

nodes.name: Ledger Accounting & Trial Balance
nodes.description: Posting to nominal ledger accounts, receivable/payable control accounts, and extracting initial trial balance.
topics: Nominal ledger architecture: T-accounts, balancing off accounts
Sales ledger and purchase ledger control accounts and reconciliation
Trial balance extraction and role as an arithmetical validation check
Differences not revealed by a trial balance (error of commission, omission, principle, etc.)
learningOutcomes: Post transactions accurately to ledger accounts.
Prepare receivables and payables ledger reconciliations.
Extract and evaluate a trial balance.
checklists: Complete control account reconciliation practice problems
Master identification of trial balance error types
resources: Relevant Acts & Standards (IFRS / ISA / Tax Acts)

stages.title: Area 3: Adjustments to Accounting Records
stages.name: Area 3: Adjustments to Accounting Records
stages.description: Accruals, prepayments, depreciation, bad debts, inventory valuation, and suspense accounts.

nodes.name: Accruals, Prepayments & Depreciation
nodes.description: Year-end period adjustments for revenue and expenses; property, plant and equipment depreciation methods (straight-line, reducing balance).
topics: Matching concept and accruals / prepayments calculations
Property, plant and equipment (IAS 16) capitalization criteria
Depreciation calculation: Straight-line vs reducing balance methods
Disposal of non-current assets and profit/loss on disposal
Asset registers and reconciliation with ledger accounts
learningOutcomes: Calculate and record year-end accruals and prepayments.
Compute depreciation charges and maintain asset schedules.
Account for non-current asset disposals and part-exchanges.
checklists: Practice 10 complex multi-period depreciation questions
Solve combined accruals and prepayments ledger problems
resources: Relevant Acts & Standards (IFRS / ISA / Tax Acts)

nodes.name: Bad Debts, Inventory & Suspense Accounts
nodes.description: Allowance for doubtful debts, inventory valuation under IAS 2 (lower of cost and NRV), and correcting errors via suspense accounts.
topics: Irrecoverable debts write-off and allowance for receivables
Inventory valuation under IAS 2: Cost determination (FIFO vs Weighted Average)
Net Realizable Value (NRV) write-downs and damaged stock adjustments
Suspense account creation, error classification, and journal adjustments
Impact of errors on reported profit and statement of financial position
learningOutcomes: Calculate allowance for doubtful debts and record adjustments.
Value closing inventory applying lower of cost and NRV rule.
Correct trial balance errors using suspense accounts and evaluate profit impact.
checklists: Solve 5 comprehensive suspense account correction problems
Practice inventory valuation under FIFO and AVCO
resources: Relevant Acts & Standards (IFRS / ISA / Tax Acts)

stages.title: Area 4: Preparing Financial Statements
stages.name: Area 4: Preparing Financial Statements
stages.description: Preparation of financial statements for sole traders, partnerships, and limited liability companies under IFRS/BFRS.

nodes.name: Sole Trader & Partnership Financial Statements
nodes.description: Preparation of Statement of Profit or Loss and Statement of Financial Position for sole proprietorships and partnerships, including partnership appropriation accounts.
topics: Sole trader final accounts: Trading, profit or loss, and balance sheet extracts
Partnership profit sharing: Interest on capital, interest on drawings, partner salaries
Partnership appropriation account and partner current/capital accounts
Admission of a partner, retirement, and goodwill adjustments at certificate level
learningOutcomes: Prepare sole trader financial statements from adjusted trial balance.
Draft partnership appropriation accounts and allocate net profit.
Maintain partner capital and current accounts.
checklists: Draft 3 full sole trader financial statements from raw trial balance
Solve 3 complete partnership profit allocation scenarios
resources: Relevant Acts & Standards (IFRS / ISA / Tax Acts)

nodes.name: Limited Company Financial Statements (IAS 1)
nodes.description: Preparation of Statement of Profit or Loss, Statement of Financial Position, and Statement of Changes in Equity for limited liability companies.
topics: Components of complete financial statements under IAS 1
Share capital, share premium, retained earnings and other reserves
Taxation in company accounts (current tax provision)
Statement of Profit or Loss format (Cost of sales, administrative, distribution expenses)
Statement of Financial Position presentation (Current vs Non-current classification)
Statement of Changes in Equity (SOCIE) preparation and dividend accounting
learningOutcomes: Specify the components of financial statements under IAS 1.
Prepare Statement of Profit or Loss and Statement of Financial Position for limited companies.
Construct Statement of Changes in Equity and account for share issues/dividends.
checklists: Complete 5 comprehensive limited company final accounts questions
Review IAS 1 presentation formats and disclosure requirements
resources: Relevant Acts & Standards (IFRS / ISA / Tax Acts)

stages.title: Area 5: Public Financial Management (PFM)
stages.name: Area 5: Public Financial Management (PFM)
stages.description: Public sector characteristics, budget systems, IPSAS overview, and public sector accounting in Bangladesh.

nodes.name: Public Sector Accounting & IFMIS
nodes.description: Differences between public and private sectors; legal framework for PFM; national budget preparation in Bangladesh; fund accounting; overview of IPSAS; Integrated Financial Management Information System (iBAS++).
topics: Characteristics of public sector vs private sector accountability
Legal and administrative framework for PFM in Bangladesh
Budget preparation steps, budget classification code (BACS), and fiscal reporting
Fund accounting principles in government organizations
Introduction to International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS)
Integrated Financial Management Information System (iBAS++ / IFMIS)
learningOutcomes: Differentiate public sector financial governance from commercial entities.
Explain the budget preparation process and classification codes in Bangladesh.
Explain the role and architecture of IFMIS/iBAS++.
checklists: Review government budgeting steps and BACS coding structure
Understand key differences between cash basis and accrual basis IPSAS
resources: Relevant Acts & Standards (IFRS / ISA / Tax Acts)
